section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The Sliding Window
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a 'filter' moving over data. Use an analogy of a magnifying glass scanning a photograph to extract specific details like edges or brightness.
section_1.example: A 3x3 'cat-ear detector' filter sliding over a pixel grid of a house pet image to highlight where the ears are located.

section_2.title: Mathematical Core: Element-wise Product and Sum
section_2.content: Define discrete convolution as the sum of element-wise products. Visually represent this as two overlapping matrices: the input matrix (A) and the kernel (K). Emphasize the 'flip and shift' mechanism (flipping the kernel) for formal definition.
section_2.example: Visual animation of a 3x3 kernel sliding over a 5x5 grid, showing the multiplication of overlapping values and the summation resulting in a single output pixel.

section_3.title: Prerequisite Sync: Dot Products
section_3.content: Briefly recap the Dot Product: the idea that the result is high only when the kernel 'matches' the underlying pattern. This ensures students understand why convolution functions as a 'feature detector'.
section_3.example: Comparing a 'vertical edge' kernel to a vertical line on a image grid—demonstrating how the high multiplication values produce a bright spot in the output.

section_4.title: Real-World Application: Image Processing & CNNs
section_4.content: Transition to modern applications. Explain how stacks of convolutions form Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Move from simple edge detection to complex object recognition.
section_4.example: A drone navigation system using a convolution layer to identify a 'landing pad' symbol on the ground amidst a noisy background.

section_5.title: Summary & Reflection
section_5.content: Recap: Convolution = Scanning + Dot Product + Feature Extraction. Encourage learners to visualize convolution as a 'template matching' engine.
section_5.example: A quick visual recap of the 'cat ear' filter evolving into a complex 'cat face' detector in deep layers.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shifted slightly right to avoid overlapping the lecture area
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Sliding Window", [
            "Think of filters as sliding magnifying glasses.",
            "Scanning photographs extracts vital visual details.",
            "Imagine our filter detecting cat ears."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        grid = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.1) for _ in range(9)]).arrange_in_grid(3, 3, buff=0.2)
        highlight = Square(side_length=0.3, color=YELLOW).move_to(grid[4])
        filter_box = Square(side_length=1.0, color=BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(grid))
        self.play(FadeIn(highlight))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(filter_box, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(filter_box))
        # Move filter box over the grid
        self.play(filter_box.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.8), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(filter_box.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.8), run_time=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.play(filter_box.animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(Indicate(filter_box))
